claims.span_literal: Specifically, SPG1 cells are enriched for MORC1, MSL3, ZBTB43, TSPAN33, TCF3, FMR1, MAGEB2, and CDK17 (Figure 2E [TSPAN33, PIWIL4, and MORC1 shown], see Table S3).
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, spermatogonia state 1 cells are enriched for MORC1, MSL3, ZBTB43, TSPAN33, TCF3, FMR1, MAGEB2, and CDK17.

claims.span_literal: Interestingly, PIWIL4 is a SPG1-specific marker for all three species (Figures 2D and 2E; Table S3).
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, PIWIL4 is a specific marker of spermatogonia state 1.

claims.span_literal: In SPG2 cells, the noncanonical markers enriched in SPG1 (described above) are diminished, whereas certain canonical markers for undifferentiated SPG increase in expression (ZBTB16 [mouse and human] and GFRA1 [all three species]), as do several noncanonical markers (DUSP6, TCF4, and L1TD1 [macaque and human only]) (Figures 2D and 2E [L1TD1 shown]; Table S3).
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, spermatogonia state 2 cells show increased expression of ZBTB16, GFRA1, DUSP6, TCF4, and L1TD1.

claims.span_literal: cells in SPG1 and SPG2 are similar to each other (Figure S2B) and at first glance express many of the well-established markers of undifferentiated SPG (e.g., GFRA1, ZBTB16 (PLZF), ITGA6, ID4, UCHL1, LIN28, DPPA4 (macaque), FGFR3, and UTF1 (human)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, undifferentiated spermatogonia (spermatogonia state 1 and spermatogonia state 2) express GFRA1, ZBTB16, ITGA6, ID4, UCHL1, LIN28, FGFR3, and UTF1.

claims.span_literal: Human and macaque SPG3-5 cells share many markers with mouse SPG3, such as DMRT1, KIT, STRA8, SOHLH1, and SOHLH2
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, differentiating spermatogonia states 3-5 express DMRT1, KIT, STRA8, SOHLH1, and SOHLH2.

claims.span_literal: Cells in macaque and human SPG4 expressed markers, such as MKI67, PCNA, numerous cyclins, DMRT1, DMRTB1, and KIT (unannotated in macaque), indicating that this population is actively proliferating
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, spermatogonia state 4 cells express MKI67, PCNA, DMRT1, DMRTB1, and KIT.

claims.span_literal: SPG6 cells turn off DMRT1 while maintaining DMRTB1 (not annotated in macaque), a specific signature of mouse type B SPG
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, spermatogonia state 6 cells turn off DMRT1 while maintaining DMRTB1.

claims.span_literal: They also begin to express many markers previously identified in mouse preleptotene spermatocytes: TEX101, LY6K, and established meiotic genes, such as SYCP2/3, SYCE1/2, MEIOB, PRDM9, SPATA22, and DNAJB11
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, spermatogonia state 6 cells begin to express TEX101, LY6K, SYCP2, SYCP3, SYCE1, SYCE2, MEIOB, PRDM9, SPATA22, and DNAJB11.

claims.span_literal: Consistent with our single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data predictions, the protein markers co-localize with UCHL1+ SPG cells lining the basement membrane of the human testis
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, UCHL1 is a marker of undifferentiated spermatogonia in the testis.

claims.span_literal: but less so with cKIT+ differentiating SPG
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, KIT is a marker of differentiating spermatogonia.

claims.span_literal: One of the most abundant populations captured in primates was peritubular myoid cells, defined by the expression of MYH11, ACTA2, collagens, laminins, versican (VCAN), and fibronectin
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, peritubular myoid cells are defined by the expression of MYH11, ACTA2, and VCAN.

claims.span_literal: The somatic compartment also contains endothelial cells (VWF, NOSTRIN, AQP1, CD34 [human]) and pericytes (MCAM, RGS5, PDGFRB, NG2, CCL2, ABCC9, and NOTCH3)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, endothelial cells express VWF, NOSTRIN, AQP1, and CD34, while pericytes express MCAM, RGS5, PDGFRB, NG2, CCL2, ABCC9, and NOTCH3.

claims.span_literal: The somatic compartment also contains endothelial cells (VWF, NOSTRIN, AQP1, CD34 [human]) and pericytes (MCAM, RGS5, PDGFRB, NG2, CCL2, ABCC9, and NOTCH3)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, pericytes express MCAM, RGS5, PDGFRB, NG2, CCL2, ABCC9, and NOTCH3.

claims.span_literal: We found the testis pericyte population splits into two distinct sub-clusters, which we annotate as muscular (m-pericytes: MCAM [higher expression], CRIP1/2, RERGL, ADIRF [unannotated in macaque], MYL9, and PTM1/2) or fibroblastic (f-pericytes: STEAP4, GUCY1A1/2, ITGA1, CD36/44 (human), collagens, and laminins)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, muscular pericytes express MCAM, CRIP1, CRIP2, RERGL, ADIRF, and MYL9, while fibroblastic pericytes express STEAP4, GUCY1A1, ITGA1, CD36, and CD44.

claims.span_literal: We found the testis pericyte population splits into two distinct sub-clusters, which we annotate as muscular (m-pericytes: MCAM [higher expression], CRIP1/2, RERGL, ADIRF [unannotated in macaque], MYL9, and PTM1/2) or fibroblastic (f-pericytes: STEAP4, GUCY1A1/2, ITGA1, CD36/44 (human), collagens, and laminins)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, fibroblastic pericytes express STEAP4, GUCY1A1, ITGA1, CD36, and CD44.

claims.span_literal: Finally, we identified two immune cell types: a major population of macrophages (CD163, HLA-DRA/MAMU-DRA, LYZ, and TYROBP) and a smaller population of T cells (CD3D, TRAC, TRBC2, and CD69)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, macrophages express CD163, HLA-DRA, LYZ, and TYROBP, while T cells express CD3D, TRAC, TRBC2, and CD69.

claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, T cells express CD3D, TRAC, TRBC2, and CD69.

claims.span_literal: we identify two molecularly distinct undifferentiated spermatogonial cell states (SPG1: TSPAN33, PIWIL4, CDK17, MORC1, ID4, and ZBTB16; SPG2: L1TD1, ID4, GFRA1, and ZBTB16)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, undifferentiated spermatogonia state 1 is marked by TSPAN33, PIWIL4, CDK17, MORC1, ID4, and ZBTB16.

claims.span_literal: we identify two molecularly distinct undifferentiated spermatogonial cell states (SPG1: TSPAN33, PIWIL4, CDK17, MORC1, ID4, and ZBTB16; SPG2: L1TD1, ID4, GFRA1, and ZBTB16)
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, undifferentiated spermatogonia state 2 is marked by L1TD1, ID4, GFRA1, and ZBTB16.

claims.span_literal: SPG6 includes type B spermatogonial cells transitioning to preleptotene spermatocytes based on the expression of conserved meiotic genes, such as PRDM9, ZCWPW1, and REC8.
claims.summary: In Homo sapiens, spermatogonia state 6 expresses the conserved meiotic genes PRDM9, ZCWPW1, and REC8.
